tasks.short: Send advertising proofs, explain them, and capture customer approval against the correct version.

steps.what: Retrieve the latest proof and match it to the campaign brief.
Check the proof for obvious errors and consistency with agreed requirements.
Send the checked proof with approval instructions and a deadline.
Explain the proof and discuss customer questions or requested changes.
Record customer approval or changes against the exact proof version.
Forward the approved version or requested changes to the creative team.

tasks.design: Configure a version-specific approval flow in the {WORKFLOW}, linking proofs in the {DOCS} to campaigns in the {CRM}. The seller checks the proof and recipient before the {EMAIL} request leaves; the customer explicitly approves that version or requests changes. Reminders and the creative handoff follow recorded status, while explanatory conversations remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attachments, customer replies and production deadlines were disconnected. Reliable version control required more coordination than sending an attachment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval flows can provide version links, reminders and audit records. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting metadata and status; no model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous replies, replacement proofs and delegated customer authority still need attention. Visual correctness and the meaning of requested changes remain human judgements.
tasks.human_edge: Explain creative choices, notice hesitation and resolve disagreements without treating silence as approval.

ambition.what: A scheduled proof clinic for first-time advertisers before their first publication deadline.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time chasing replies and locating versions, leaving room for first-time advertiser support. Publication and customer approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Release an approved advertising booking to production.
reach.learn: Version identifiers, publication cut-offs and the difference between approval and a change request.

evidence.claim: Version-specific approval requests, reminders and status-based handoffs can use deterministic workflow configuration.
The effort shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: Proofs have stable campaign and version identifiers.
The reference workflow includes substantive customer discussion; simple repeat proofs may need none.
Customer approval uses an explicit version-specific action; email exceptions return to the seller.
Build ranges are working effort for one pilot workflow. Access and any employee consultation under national rules can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether the existing {WORKFLOW} supports external approvals and immutable proof versions.
Who may approve for each customer and how delegation is verified.
How often approval arrives through email, telephone or an agency.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Does a version-specific approval link reduce clarification without confusing occasional customers?
Which proof metadata checks can prevent wrong-version delivery reliably?
new_work: Maintain approval templates, customer permissions and escalation deadlines.
Handle ambiguous replies, expired links and replacement proofs.
Review failed reminders and missing creative handoffs.

tasks.short: Process account correspondence, prepare paperwork, and pass accepted advertising bookings to operations.

steps.what: Read incoming account correspondence and identify the required action.

loop.output: Suggested action, extracted references and a source-linked summary.
loop.check: Validate the action against allowed categories and require source spans for extracted facts.
loop.stop: One pass and one validation retry per message; ambiguous requests enter the seller's exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle known senders and document types, but free-text requests mix changes, questions and acceptance.

steps.what: Match the correspondence to the correct customer and opportunity.
Check booking, billing and contact fields for completeness.
Fill standard booking forms, agreements and account letters from approved templates.
Resolve missing information and disputed terms with the customer.
Check commercial authority and approve the final paperwork.
Send approved paperwork to the customer for acceptance.
File the correspondence, issued paperwork and customer acceptance against the account.
Enter accepted booking details and billing references in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Connect the {EMAIL}, {CRM}, {DOCS} and {ERP} through the {WORKFLOW}, using identifiers, required fields and approved document templates. A bounded model classifies unfamiliar correspondence; deterministic checks match records, generate paperwork and prevent duplicate bookings. The authorised approver clears commercial commitments before sending, and customer acceptance must be verified before an accepted booking reaches the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free-text requests obscured otherwise structured transactions. Missing identifiers and different booking fields made manual copying the practical fallback.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can turn correspondence into reviewable suggestions. Existing configuration and faster connector development handle the structured work without autonomous agents.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial exceptions, legal wording and uncertain customer acceptance need people. GDPR requires appropriate access, purpose and retention controls for correspondence.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a negotiation from acceptance and resolve disputed commitments without losing the customer relationship.

ambition.what: A guided first-booking paperwork service for small advertisers without an agency.

tasks.altitude: The seller handles exceptions and first-booking support instead of copying fields. Standard bookings can progress within delegated limits; contract exceptions and credit decisions retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Validate an advertising booking before billing and production.
reach.learn: Booking identifiers, customer acceptance evidence, billing references and duplicate prevention.
Discount authority, unusual cancellation terms and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Teamleader supports customer records and online quote signing; its Focus AI acts after approval.
Templates, field validation and idempotent integrations can automate standard account paperwork without an agent.
The effort shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: The reference process covers routine correspondence through accepted booking; not every message creates an order.
Exact identifiers permit automatic matching. Ambiguous matches and nonstandard acceptance evidence require review.
The authorised sales approver is the seller within delegated limits and the sales manager for exceptions.
The time split includes the order clerk's final handoff work.
Build ranges cover one booking route. Access and employee consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: The actual contract, discount, credit and booking approval limits.
Whether the {CRM} and {ERP} expose supported interfaces and shared identifiers.
Which customer acceptance methods are valid for each agreement type.
The volume of amendments, cancellations, unmatched messages and duplicate records.
Applicable retention periods, access permissions and national employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which correspondence categories can be recognised reliably enough to reduce review?
Which acceptance checks prevent false booking creation across different document formats?
new_work: Review ambiguous correspondence, record matches and customer acceptance evidence.
Maintain templates, required fields and approval routing.
Resolve rejected transfers and reconcile bookings between the {CRM} and {ERP}.
Review permissions, retention settings and connector failures.

tasks.short: Develop promotional plans with internal stakeholders and advertising agencies.

steps.what: Review account objectives, commercial commitments and current opportunities.
Review campaign delivery, audience and performance reports.
Read agency briefs and internal priorities before the planning discussion.

loop.input: Agency brief and internal priorities, alongside validated commercial and performance facts.
loop.output: Source-linked objectives, constraints, disagreements and open questions.
loop.check: Require source references; verify figures against structured inputs and flag conflicting instructions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per brief; unresolved conflicts remain explicit questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives and constraints appear in varied prose and can conflict across stakeholders.

steps.what: Discuss promotional options, stakeholder priorities and practical trade-offs.
Write the proposed plan, including objectives, activities, budget assumptions and responsibilities.

loop.input: Seller-entered planning decisions, validated facts and an approved plan template.
loop.output: A promotional plan draft with explicit assumptions, owners and unresolved items.
loop.check: Recalculate budgets deterministically; trace commitments to decisions and mark missing owners or dates.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported commitments are removed or returned to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but expressing the agreed rationale requires bounded writing.

steps.what: Approve the plan's budget and commercial commitments with the sales manager.

tasks.design: Assemble a planning pack from the {CRM}, {BI} and approved briefs in the {DOCS}, using deterministic retrieval and a bounded extraction loop. People negotiate direction; a separate bounded writing loop turns their entered decisions into a plan, with code checking totals and missing fields. Budget and commercial commitments take effect only after the appropriate human approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant facts were scattered, while the valuable part of planning depended on negotiation. Automating the whole task would have confused preparation with decision-making.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured retrieval and bounded drafting can remove preparation and documentation effort. They do not require a breakthrough in strategic judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders can disagree about goals, attribution and acceptable risk. Comparable audience and performance figures may be expensive to establish across media.
tasks.human_edge: Read competing interests, challenge weak assumptions and secure commitments that stakeholders will honour.

ambition.what: Quarterly promotion clinics for smaller agency accounts.

tasks.altitude: The seller can prepare more useful planning sessions and follow through on decisions. They gain a stronger basis for recommendations; budget and inventory commitments still require delegated authority or manager approval.

reach.learn: Contribution margin, inventory constraints and how to compare competing account opportunities.

reach.task: Turn a customer objective into a measurable service proposal.
reach.learn: Outcome definitions, attribution limits and explicit assumptions.

evidence.claim: Structured fact retrieval and template-based planning can be separated from human negotiation and strategic judgement.
Bounded extraction and drafting can support planning documents when facts and commitments are checked separately.
The effort shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: The seller sells media inventory and promotional packages, rather than controlling the customer's full marketing budget.
The reference company has campaign reports available through the {BI}.
Meeting decisions are entered by the seller; recording or scoring employees is outside this design.
Build ranges cover one planning template and reporting route. Access and any consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which audience and campaign measures are comparable across the company's media.
Who approves promotional budgets, discounts and inventory commitments.
Whether agency materials may be processed by the proposed model service.
Which smaller accounts would value a planning clinic.
Which national employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which planning-pack fields most improve the quality of stakeholder decisions?
Can reviewers reliably detect unsupported commitments in the generated plan?
new_work: Validate performance definitions and update planning templates.
Review extracted constraints and generated plans.
Resolve conflicting briefs and missing decisions.
Monitor stale data and changes to reporting access.

tasks.short: Recommend advertising media and prepare sample advertisements for customer presentations.

steps.what: Clarify the customer's audience, objective, budget and creative constraints.
Compare media-kit audiences, formats and indicative prices.
Select the medium and explain its fit with the customer's objective.
Draft sample copy or a storyboard for the selected medium.

loop.input: Campaign brief, selected medium, brand guidelines and approved claims.
loop.output: Sample copy or storyboard with claim references and unresolved placeholders.
loop.check: Check length and required wording mechanically; the seller checks accuracy, tone and claim support.
loop.stop: At most two candidates and one revision; unresolved claims remain placeholders for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle format, but new customer-specific copy requires bounded writing.

steps.what: Assemble the sample in a creative production application using brand assets.
Check the sample's claims, brand fit, readability and presentation readiness.
Present the recommendation and sample, then discuss customer reactions.

tasks.design: Maintain structured media specifications, rates and audience definitions in the {CRM}, and generate a comparison using deterministic filters and calculations. A bounded writing loop drafts copy from approved material in the {DOCS}; a template renderer on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles sample advertisements from approved assets. The seller chooses the recommendation and approves the sample before presenting it; final production proof approval follows separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Media information and creative assets were disconnected, so preparing even a simple sample involved repeated lookup and layout work. Recommendations also depended on judgement that could not be reduced to price filters.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster development makes a narrow media catalogue and template renderer economical. A bounded writing loop can propose copy without choosing the medium or making unsupported performance promises.
tasks.still_hard: Audience figures can be incomparable and availability can change. Bespoke audio, video, illustration and sensitive claims still need specialist work and asset-rights checks.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a persuasive medium, recognise weak audience assumptions and adapt the explanation to the customer's commercial context.

ambition.what: A first-campaign comparison session showing two suitable media options with tailored samples.

tasks.altitude: The seller can spend more time comparing viable options with customers and less time assembling samples. They gain faster preparation, while pricing exceptions, inventory commitments and publication approval keep their existing decision rights.

reach.task: Validate whether a proposed advertising format meets technical requirements.
reach.learn: Dimensions, duration, file limits, accessibility requirements and the difference between a sample and production-ready creative.

reach.task: Demonstrate alternative formats to a customer.
reach.learn: How to compare options clearly without implying unsupported performance guarantees.

evidence.claim: Structured media filtering, rate calculations and template rendering can use deterministic code.
Customer-specific sample copy can use bounded drafting with human checks for claims, tone and suitability.
The effort shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: The pilot covers a small catalogue of repeatable formats and approved brand assets.
Broadcast samples can be scripts or storyboards; finished audio and video production are outside the initial renderer.
The seller prepares simple samples; bespoke creative work goes to the creative team.
Sample advertisements are illustrative and do not constitute publication approval.
Build ranges cover one catalogue and template family. Access and any consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which media formats, audience definitions and availability sources the company uses.
Whether rate cards and specifications exist in structured form.
Who prepares samples today and which creative production application is used.
Which assets and claims are approved for reuse.
Which customer data may enter the model service and which national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which template family covers enough routine samples to justify deterministic rendering?
How should comparisons show incompatible audience measures without implying false precision?
Which review checks catch misleading claims and layout failures before presentation?
new_work: Maintain the media catalogue, rate rules and sample templates.
Review draft copy and replace unsupported claims.
Test rendered samples after specification or template changes.
Maintain approved assets, reuse permissions and specialist escalation routes.

role.altitude: The advertising sales agent spends more of the week interpreting customer goals, comparing media and resolving commercial uncertainty. Faster preparation supports smaller accounts, while binding terms, budget changes and publication still follow delegated authority and explicit approvals.
reach: Order clerk: validate accepted bookings and production handoffs.
Sales manager: frame commercial exceptions and promotional allocation decisions.
Sales engineer: assess technical feasibility of advertising formats.
Demonstrator and product promoter: make media comparisons understandable to customers.
skills_to_grow: Compare audience evidence and explain attribution limits.
Translate customer objectives into clear briefs and measurable plans.
Recognise commercial authority limits and acceptance evidence.
Review generated copy for claim support and brand suitability.
Use version control, structured records and exception queues.
Handle customer information under GDPR and applicable national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer smaller advertisers a guided first-campaign service: clarify goals, compare two suitable media options, show tailored samples and guide approval through to a validated booking.
